function.description: Send a GET request to a specified URL to retrieve all products and branches with triangulation runs in the latest 90 days. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The MIME types that are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request as a dictionary of header names to header values.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

days.description: The number of days to look back for triangulation runs.

end_date.description: The end date for the data retrieval period, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. If null, defaults to the current date.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the request.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to a certificate file to verify the peer.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names to cookie values.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary mapping protocol names to URLs of the proxies.

stream.description: If true, the response should be streamed; otherwise, the response will be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not.

message.content:
**Triangulation Metrics – A Quick Overview** | What | Why it matters | |------|----------------| | **Definition** | Quantitative measures derived from *triangulation*, i.e., determining positions or distances based on angles measured at known reference points. In practice this often means computing straight‑line distances (“as‑the‑air” or “great‑circle”) between two geographic locations given their latitude/longitude pairs. | | **Typical Calculations** | • Haversine / Vincenty formulas
• Law of Cosines (for planar approximations)
• Spherical trigonometry (law of sines & cosines)
• Ellipsoidal geodesic solutions (e.g., Karney’s algorithm) | | **Common Inputs** | Latitude & longitude of each point (decimal degrees), optional altitude if you’re doing 3D triangulation.
Optional Earth ellipsoid parameters (WGS84, GRS80). | | **Key Outputs** | • Great‑circle distance (km/miles)
• Initial bearing / azimuth (degrees East of North)
• Final bearing (if needed)
• Cross‑track errors when comparing against a path segment | | **Why It Matters** | • Navigation & routing (aviation, maritime, road networks)
• Geospatial analytics (GIS, remote sensing)
• Surveying & land parcel delineation
• Robotics & autonomous vehicle localization | --- ### How It Works (Simplified) 1. **Convert Coordinates** Convert lat/lon into radians (or Cartesian XYZ if working on an ellipsoid). 2. **Apply Formula** For most practical purposes we use the Haversine formula: \[ d = 2R\arcsin\!\Bigl(\sqrt{\sin^2\frac{Δφ}{2}+cos φ_1\,cos φ_2\,\sin^2\frac{Δλ}{2}}\Bigr) \] where \( R ≈ 6371 km \) (Earth radius), Δφ = φ₂−φ₁, Δλ = λ₂−λ₁. 3. **Compute Bearing** \[ θ = atan2( sin Δλ·cos φ_2,\ cos φ_1·sin φ_2 - sin φ_1·cos φ_2·cos Δλ ) \] Normalize to [0°,360°]. 4. **Return Results** Distance + bearings give you full triangulation metrics. --- ### Accuracy Considerations | Factor | Impact | Mitigation | |--------|-------|------------| | **Choice of Ellipsoid** | WGS84 vs local datum differences (~10–20 m) | Use appropriate datum for your region | | **Altitude Ignored** | Over long vertical gradients (<100 m) negligible | Include elevation if required | | **Floating‑Point Precision** | Small rounding errors accumulate over many hops | Double precision arithmetic | | **Sensor Noise** | GPS multipath, atmospheric delays | Kalman filtering, differential corrections | --- ### Typical Applications | Domain | Example Metric Usage | |--------|---------------------| | Aviation | Compute flight legs, heading adjustments, fuel planning | | Maritime | Determine shortest sea routes, calculate drift relative to currents | | Surveying | Verify boundary lines, compute area via triangulated network | | Autonomous Vehicles | Cross‑check LiDAR/Radar-derived paths against map-based great‑circle segments | | Geoscience | Estimate seismic wave travel times along great circles | --- #### Bottom Line *Triangulation metrics* are essentially the set of numerical outputs you get after applying spherical/trigonometrical geometry to determine distances and directions between two points on Earth's surface. These numbers form the backbone of everything from simple “distance calculator” apps to complex route optimization engines in aviation and shipping logistics.
